content: 1. The combination of buprenorphine subdermal implant and hydroxychloroquine sulfate can lead to an increased QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. The concurrent use of buprenorphine transdermal and hydroxychloroquine sulfate also increases the QTc interval. Avoid or consider alternative medications. 3. Buprenorphine long-acting injection and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both elevate the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 4. Canakinumab and hydroxychloroquine sulfate together enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Ceritinib and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative medications. 6. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of hydroxychloroquine sulfate by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but caution is advised. 7. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and chlorpromazine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 9. Immunosuppressive therapies, including radiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, and corticosteroids (at supraphysiologic doses), may diminish the immune response to the cholera vaccine. 10. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ciltacabtagene autoleucel both enhance each other's immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 11. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 12. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases the toxicity of cisapride by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 13. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and citalopram both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative medications. 14. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 15. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and clofazimine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 16. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and clomipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or consider alternative medications. 17. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and clozapine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and crizotinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 19. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases the level or effect of cyclosporine via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and dapsone topical have an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining dapsone topical with oral dapsone or antimalarial medications due to the risk of hemolytic reactions. 21. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and dasatinib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 22. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and degarelix both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 23. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the dengue vaccine due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and denosumab require caution in patients on concomitant immunosuppressants or with impaired immune systems due to an increased risk of serious infections. Monitor closely. 25. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and desflurane both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 26. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and desipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative medications. 27. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and deutetrabenazine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically significant extent. However, certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 28. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases digoxin levels through an unknown mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of diphtheria and tetanus toxoids via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 30. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of diphtheria, tetanus toxoids, and acellular pertussis vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 31. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of diphtheria, tetanus toxoids, acellular pertussis, and inactivated poliovirus vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 32. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and disopyramide both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 33. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and dofetilide both prolong the QTc interval. Dofetilide increases the toxicity of hydroxychloroquine sulfate by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 34. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and dolasetron both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 35. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate increases and echinacea decreases immunosuppressive effects, leading to an unclear interaction. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and efavirenz both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 41. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and eliglustat both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 42. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and encorafenib both prolong the QTc interval. Encorafenib is associated with dose-dependent QTc prolongation. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 43. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and entrectinib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 44. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and escitalopram both increase the QTc interval. Escitalopram increases the toxicity of hydroxychloroquine sulfate by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 50. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and etanercept both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 51. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and etrasimod both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Etrasimod may cause transient decreases in heart rate and AV conduction delays when initiated. 52. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and everolimus both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 53. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and ezogabine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 54. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and fexinidazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of fexinidazole with drugs known to block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval. 55. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and fingolimod both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 56. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and flecainide both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 57. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 58. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and formoterol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 61. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and foscarnet both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 62. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and fostemsavir both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 63. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and gemifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 64. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and gemtuzumab both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 65. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and gepirone both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 66. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and gilteritinib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 67. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. If unavoidable, obtain ECGs at baseline, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 68. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and glasdegib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 69. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and glatiramer both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 70. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and golimumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 71. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and granisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 72. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and haloperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 73. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis A vaccine (inactivated) via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 74. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis A/B vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 75. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis A/typhoid vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 76. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis B vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 77. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the human papillomavirus vaccine (nonavalent) via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Immunosuppressive therapies, including radiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, and corticosteroids (at supraphysiologic doses), may reduce immune responses to vaccines. 78. Hydroxyzine and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 79. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and idecabtagene vicleucel both enhance each other's immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 81. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and infliximab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 85.
